May, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:10058

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti
 On The 6 th Of May, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 211 of 2005
 National Insurance Co.Ltd.
 Versus
 The State Of M.P.And Ors.
 Appearance:
 Shri Kamal S.Rochlani - Advocate for the appellant/Insu
 Company.
 Shri B.M. Patel- Ga for respondent No. 1/State.
 Order
Appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
challenging the award the dated 19/11/2004 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind in
Claim Case

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: No. 39/2002, whereby, an amount of Rs. 2,70,859.80/- has been awarded towards damage caused to the vehicle in question.

2. The facts in nutshell are that the TATA truck 1210 bearing registration no. MP 03 1010 was owned by M.P. Police Department (hereinafter shall be referred to as "the Police Vehicle") and was allotted to 17 Battalion SAF, Bhind.

The Police Vehicle met with an accident during the intervening night of 27-28/2/1996 with another truck bearing registration no. GJ 1 U 3967 (hereinafter shall be referred to as "the offending vehicle").
As a result of this accident, the driver of the Police Vehicle died and the truck NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10058 2 MA-211-2005 suffered damages.
This appeal is concerning to the claim lodged by respondent no. 1 in respect of the damages caused to the Police Vehicle due to aforesaid accident.
It is no more in dispute that the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no. 2 while it was driven by respondent no. 3 at the time of accident.
It is also no more in dispute that offending vehicle was insured with appellant/Insurance Company.

3. Respondent no. 1 lodged a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming a compensation of Rs. 3,85,859.80/- towards the expenses to be incurred for repairing of the Police Vehicle.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs. 2,70,859.80/- with interest @6% per annum on the said amount from the date of filing of claim petition.
The appellant/Insurance Company has been held liable to pay the aforesaid amount.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has challenged the impugned award on the ground that there was no proof of damage caused to the Police Vehicle and the amount has been awarded by the Tribunal solely relying upon the estimate of repairs (Ex. P/3C) submitted by Dealer namely SG Motors.

Learned counsel submitted that firstly the said estimate was not proved by any competent witness who has examined the truck and assessed the damages; secondly, the Company is liable to reimburse the amount which is actually incurred for repairing of the truck.
However, in the instant case, admittedly, the truck was not repaired and only the expected amount which may be required for its repair is claimed.
He also submits that the estimate prepared by Dealer is wholly vague on the face of it.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10058 3 MA-211-2005 5.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State supported the impugned award and submitted that the Insurance Company failed to lead any evidence in rebuttal, and therefore, the Tribunal was justified in accepting the estimate prepared by the Dealer.
He further submitted that the truck was not repaired as the amount to be incurred was huge and therefore, the Department was waiting for the amount to be received from the Insurance Company.
He also submitted that the Dealer was competent to give the estimate of repairs, and therefore, in absence of any contrary evidence, the same is rightly accepted by the Tribunal.

6. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
7.
The amount awarded by the Tribunal towards repair of the Police Vehicle is solely based upon the estimate of repairs prepared by SG Motors, which has been exhibited as Ex. P/3C.
The aforesaid document of estimate has been proved before the Tribunal by the Officers of the respondent/Department.
No witness has been examined in support of the aforesaid estimate, who has actually examined the damage caused to the Police Vehicle and has prepared the estimate.

8. This Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Union of India and Ors. (M.A.No.
1088 of 2014)

sentences.text: decided on 1st of April, 2025, had an occasion to examine the similar situation and in para 9 it is held thus:-
" 9 . The alternate submission of counsel for the appellant - company is also required to be examined.

The damages of Rs.5 Lacs assessed by the Tribunal is solely based upon the document which is marked as Ex.P-25, work estimate prepared by Vikram Motors Pvt. Ltd., which is stated to be a dealer of Swaraz Mazda Vehicle.

In support of this estimate, the claimants/respondents have not examined the surveyor/mechanic or the person who has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10058 4 MA-211-2005 prepared this estimate.
Further, the note appended to this estimate also makes it clear that this is not the actual determination of damage caused to the vehicle and it is only based upon the assumption and presumption.
The estimate also does not give the bifurcation of the damage caused to the vehicle and the necessary repairs required for the same.

Therefore, this document, which prepared after lapse of three months of the accident, does not inspire confidence and is also not acceptable to sustain the alleged loss caused to the vehicle of respondent no.1 & 2.

Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal assessing damage of Rs.5 Lacs on the National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs The State Of M.P.And Ors. on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66104849/
2 basis of Ex.P-25 is also not sustainable in law."

sentences.text:
9. Thus, in view of the aforesaid legal position, it cannot be said that the estimate of repairs, Ex.
P/3C is the actual amount of expenses required to be incurred for repair of the Police Vehicle.

10. The another argument of the counsel for the Insurance Company is that the Company is required to reimburse the amount which has been actually incurred by the Claimants for repair of the Police Vehicle.
Admittedly, in this case, the repairing was not carried out and the claim petition was filed on the expected expenses to be incurred.

In this regard, the provisions of Section 147 (1) (a) and (b)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are relevant and is produced hereunder:-
"147. Requirement of policies and limits of liability.-

(1)In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which-- (a) is issued by a person who is an authorised insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section (2)--
(i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person, including owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in a public place;
(ii)against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a public service vehicle caused by or arising out of the use of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10058 5 MA-211-2005 vehicle in a public place."
11.
Thus, by reading the aforesaid provision, it is clear that the amount to be reimbursed by the Insurance Company should be the actual amount already spent by the Claimants towards repair.
12. Thus, in view of the aforesaid legal position, the award passed by the Tribunal is unsustainable in law and is liable to be and accordingly set aside.
13. Appeal stands allowed and disposed of.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE JPS/-
